name: Massachusetts
agency: Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV), MassDOT
permitAge: 16 (learner's permit valid up to 2 years; parent/guardian signs the application if under 18)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours certified by parent/guardian (30 if a driver skills development program is completed), plus driver ed: 30 h classroom, 12 h behind the wheel, 6 h observation, 2 h parent class (unless taken in the past 5 years)
teen.holdPermit: 6 consecutive months with a clean record before the road test (a suspension restarts the clock); JOL from age 16 1/2
teen.nightLimit: Permit holders under 18: no driving 12 a.m.-5 a.m. unless a licensed parent/guardian with 1 year of experience is present. JOL: no driving 12:30-5 a.m. unless a parent/guardian is present
teen.passengerLimit: JOL first 6 months: no passengers under 18 except immediate family unless a licensed driver 21+ with 1 year experience is beside the driver
teen.phone: Under 18: no mobile phone or device at all, even hands-free, except to report an emergency (c.90 s.8M). All drivers: hands-free only since Feb 23, 2020

notes: Supervisor for permit: licensed driver 21+ with at least 1 year of experience in the seat beside the driver
JOL penalties: first speeding offense 90-day suspension (1 year subsequent); first passenger/night violation 60 days, second 180 days, then 1 year

Speed (c.90 s.17): thickly settled/business district 30 mph (towns may set 25 on local roads); school zone 20; outside thickly settled: divided highway 50, undivided 40; 65 only on named interstate segments
Rotary: entering vehicles yield to vehicles already in the rotary (c.89 s.8)
Right on red after stop unless posted; left on red allowed from one-way onto one-way (c.89 s.8)
Headlights required whenever wipers are needed (since April 7, 2015); daytime running lights do not count
School bus: stop from either direction; only exception is opposite direction on a highway divided by a physical barrier; may not follow within 100 feet of a school bus
Move Over (c.89 s.7C): change to a lane not adjacent to stationary emergency/maintenance/recovery vehicle, or slow down; S.2642 (2025) expansion passed Senate, enactment not confirmed
Compulsory insurance: four coverages incl. PIP; minimums raised July 1, 2025 (25k/50k BI, 30k PD, 8k PIP per mass.gov - one page still lists older amounts)
RMV suspends after 3 surchargeable events in 2 years

Checked 2026-10-09 against the Massachusetts Driver's Manual, Revised April 2026 (PDF modified 2026-08-21); printed page = PDF page - 8. Exam: 25 questions, 18 correct to pass, 25 minutes (p16); Class D/M exam in 36 languages plus English, with audio in all of them (p17)
Manual (p79) gives defaults: 20 school zone, 30 thickly settled/business (25 where signed), 40 outside thickly settled, 50 on a highway outside thickly settled
